clue.text: Endangered species in the Guardian record — about time — look!

parts.note: a clue printed in the Guardian is here, so being in the Guardian is being here

indicators.note: about means around, so the record wraps around the time

parts.note: a diary is a daily record
to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the newspaper's records show some creature is facing extinction, and look at the date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T inside DIARY to give DITARY. 'In the Guardian' means 'here', since the clue appears in that paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary members of the House of Lords have been mostly abolished, so the few left are jokingly a species facing extinction.

clue.text: NHS monopoly in bed-making?

definitions.meaning: the National Health Service, Britain's public health system, has a corner (sole control) on the hospital market
a neat fold tucked under the mattress at each end of a made bed, as nurses do it

explanation.definitionFit: A tight hospital-style tuck in the sheets is standard bed-making jargon; cornering a market means owning it, so hospitals are the NHS's monopoly.

clue.text: Prepared to end in study

indicators.note: in places the phrase for ending inside the word for study

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: Someone got ready to finish their life in a quiet study room.
explanation.definitionFit: Readied is a simple synonym of prepared, made ready.

clue.text: Any problem with Wilde's journal?

indicators.note: a problem with the letters signals that they are to be put into another order

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter, so Wilde's gives WILDES

explanation.surface: A question whether anything is wrong with Oscar Wilde's diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges the letters of ANY and WILDES. 'Wilde's journal' looks like Oscar Wilde's diary, but 'journal' here means a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily newspaper is a journal; the Daily News is the name of several real papers.

clue.text: Eliminate unwanted sounds from 1 2 2 (said the archbishop)

indicators.note: from here means the answer is made out of the letters that follow, rearranged

parts.note: the figure 1 is the word one

indicators.note: Archbishop Desmond Tutu's name is how two, two sounds when said out loud

parts.note: two twos in a row, spoken, sound like the archbishop's surname

explanation.surface: An archbishop talks about filtering out noise from a sequence of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Archbishop Desmond Tutu's surname sounds like 'two two'. 'from' is only a loose anagram signal, and the fodder is itself indirect; the blog grumbles about both.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune out is to stop hearing a noise, as you turn a radio dial away from interference.

clue.text: Free from duty and anxiety

parts.note: one verb covers both: taking over a sentry's watch so they can leave, and easing someone's worry

explanation.definitionFit: To relieve a guard is to replace them, freeing them from duty; to relieve worry is to ease it.

clue.text: See 17
Seek to resurrect cry of Bacchae about moggy

indicators.note: about means around, so the cry wraps around the cat

parts.note: evoe was the cry of joy shouted by the Bacchae, followers of Bacchus
moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat

explanation.surface: Bacchus's wild women shout around a pet cat to bring something back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bacchae, the frenzied women followers of Bacchus, shouted 'Evoe!' in worship; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To evocate is to summon a spirit, as a necromancer calls up the dead, so it is to try to bring back.

clue.text: Nasty, messy and last (possibly) operations I scrutinise

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a nasty and messy job, and maybe the last one too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of NASTY, MESSY and LAST together. The definition is spoken by the analyst: 'I examine operations'.
explanation.definitionFit: A systems analyst studies how an organisation's processes work, so they examine its operations.

clue.text: See 17
Talk of cattle and dog, this is footpad's work

parts.note: cattle low, so their talk is lowing
Toby is the dog in the old British Punch and Judy puppet show

explanation.surface: Cows mooing and a dog barking: the noises a highway robber hears at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Toby is the dog in Punch and Judy, a traditional British seaside puppet show.
explanation.definitionFit: Low toby was old thieves' slang for robbing people on foot, as footpads (highwaymen without horses) did.

clue.text: Island given the chop in an unfriendly way

indicators.note: given the chop means beheaded, so the island loses its first letter

parts.note: Sicily is the Italian island

explanation.surface: An island loses its funding in a cold-hearted manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the chop' cuts the S off the front of SICILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something icily means doing it coldly, without warmth or friendliness.

clue.text: With Queen coming in unexpectedly, crave to magnify response

indicators.note: coming in means the queen's letters go inside the other letters
unexpectedly suggests the letters come out in an unforeseen order

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: When the Queen walks in by surprise, someone longs to make a bigger fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges CRAVE TO, and 'coming in' puts ER inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to respond more strongly than needed, exaggerating your reaction.

clue.text: See 20
Fancy 250,000 sheets?

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500; multiplying it by the next piece gives the clue's figure
a ream is 500 sheets of paper, and 500 times 500 is 250,000

explanation.surface: A question whether a huge pile of paper is just a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: D (500) next to REAM (500 sheets) reads as 500 times 500 sheets. The blog notes the printed clue once read '2,500 sheets'; 250,000 is the correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a daydream or idle wish, the sense of the noun dream.

clue.text: Protection without hesitation — of young trees etc

definitions.text: Protection without hesitation — of young trees etc

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the protection goes around the hesitation

parts.note: defence is protection
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Guarding saplings and similar plants must be done promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not 'lacking', so nothing is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A deer fence is high fencing that keeps deer from eating saplings and other plants, a kind of protection.

clue.text: Talk of cattle for sale (still talking)

indicators.note: talk of means the word for cattle is said aloud

parts.note: cows are cattle

explanation.surface: A salesman keeps chatting about cows on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a sailing town on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast. '(still talking)' means 'for sale' is also heard spoken: 'for sail'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowes is famous for yachting, home of Cowes Week regatta, so it is the place to go for sail, said out loud.

clue.text: Galloway's time to have more hair on top

indicators.note: on top places the hair piece above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: a wig gives you more hair
to own is to have

explanation.surface: A Scot from Galloway reckons it's time to grow a fuller head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Wigtown is a town in Galloway, south-west Scotland, so it is one of Galloway's places.

clue.text: Iconic building, that of Tate Britain, which needs control of the waves to stop

indicators.note: a loose signal that the letters of the gallery's name are made into something else

parts.note: taken as written
BR is an abbreviation for Britain or British
sea power is naval control of the oceans
a station is a stopping place

explanation.surface: A famous London landmark like the Tate's needs Britannia to rule the waves before it can stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that of' is a weak anagram signal: TATE and BR rearrange to BATTER. Then come SEA POWER and STATION. The blog also calls the signal dodgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea Power Station is the four-chimneyed former power plant on the Thames, one of London's best-known buildings.

clue.text: Vales sleep

definitions.meaning: vale is Latin for farewell, so vales are goodbyes
childish word for sleep or bedtime, as in 'off to ...'

explanation.definitionFit: The doubled goodbye can mean farewells, and in nursery talk it also means going to sleep.

clue.text: I'm in the wrong place for one who painted a queen in the 14 across

indicators.note: in the wrong place means the letter I is moved to another position

parts.note: Titian was the great Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A painter, out of position, says he portrayed a queen in his reverie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm in the wrong place' tells you to move the I in TITIAN to give TITANI; add A. 14 across is DREAM, so the queen is the fairy queen in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Genuine engineers follow later

indicators.note: follow puts the engineers after the word for later

parts.note: since can mean later, as in 'he has since left'
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: The real engineers will turn up afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means honest and heartfelt, so genuine.

clue.text: Just abandoned with recent development all over the place

parts.note: right means just or fair
left means abandoned
and means with or plus

indicators.note: development suggests the word recent is worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Justice is abandoned and recent changes leave everything in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Right, left and centre is an idiom meaning everywhere, in every direction.

clue.text: Figure there's too much translated to English

parts.note: trop is French for too much, so the phrase is translated into French

explanation.surface: Someone says the figures have too much rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' tells you to use French: TROP means too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, such as a metaphor.

clue.text: Affectionate letter from Henry to Jane?

parts.note: fond means affectionate
A is simply a letter

explanation.surface: A loving letter sent from Henry to Jane.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Fonda was the actor; Jane Fonda is his daughter. The surface wants a love letter between two people.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry and Jane Fonda, father and daughter, were both film stars, so the family surname runs from one to the other.

clue.text: End of the company's keeping record of green study

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word
keeping means holding the record inside

parts.note: Coy is a military abbreviation for company
a log is a record

explanation.surface: The end of the firm's practice of keeping environmental research records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of the' gives E. 'keeping' puts LOG inside COY, the army abbreviation for company.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecology is the study of living things and their surroundings, which green politics draws on.

clue.text: Hermia was offered this or death; Ophelia chose death

definitions.text: Hermia was offered this or death; Ophelia chose death

parts.words: Hermia was offered this or death; Ophelia chose death
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Hermia must marry, die or become a nun; Hamlet tells Ophelia to go and join nuns, and she drowns

explanation.definitionFit: A nunnery is a convent, the fate Hermia is offered and that Hamlet tells Ophelia to enter.

clue.text: Where to put signature for meiosis

definitions.meaning: you sign your name below a document, so beneath what it says
in rhetoric meiosis is a figure that makes something seem smaller than it is

explanation.definitionFit: Meiosis is the rhetorical figure of deliberately playing things down; read literally, the answer is the space below a document.
